dimensions.reasons: Group A cam_submitted.png and wide_high.png do show the basic category of scene: a dark rider standing on a green-blue snowboard over a snowy incline, with blue boot/binding forms and a few rocks. However, the rider is a very small low-poly mannequin in a broad landscape rather than the close, moving snowboarder framing of the reference.
issues: The reference's realistic close framing, crouched carving pose, and progressively lifted board are not reproduced.
The background is a sparse smooth snow hill with isolated faceted boulders rather than a steep, snow-patched rocky bank.
No visible powder spray, carved track, or board-tail kick-up appears in any submitted view.
The submitted character lacks the recognizable clothing and body detail of the reference rider.

dimensions.reasons: The board, bindings, boots, and legs are generally arranged as a supported standing assembly in detail_rider.png, and the board sits plausibly at the snow surface. The terrain itself is coherent and continuous.
issues: A small brown cuboid visibly floats beside the torso/upper legs in detail_helmet.png and detail_rider.png with no apparent attachment.
The rigid segmented limbs and torso create a mannequin-like construction rather than a believable flexible snowboarder.
The visible stance is mostly upright and board-flat, without convincing edge loading or a plausible carving interaction with the snow.

dimensions.reasons: The color cues are partly right: wide_high.png and detail_rider.png show a dark rider, a teal-green board, and vivid blue boot/binding areas that correspond broadly to the reference palette.
issues: The rider reads as a blocky articulated mannequin rather than a person in padded jacket, loose snow pants, gloves, helmet, and goggles.
The board has sharp angular slab-like ends instead of the smoothly rounded snowboard silhouette in the reference.
The helmet and goggles are not clearly modeled; only a small red-orange accent is visible near the dark head in wide_high.png.
Boots and bindings are simplified as chunky blue rectangular forms, missing their black, white, strapped construction.

dimensions.reasons: The snow surface and cast shadows create a coherent rendered outdoor environment, especially in cam_submitted.png and wide_high.png. Nevertheless, the dominant visual result is an untextured low-poly previz rather than a believable snowboard shot.
issues: The faceted body, rocks, and board are visibly artificial and lack the silhouette detail necessary for a convincing rider.
Several views are washed out and low contrast, notably detail_board.png, wide_front.png, and wide_side.png.
The snow's repeated wavy markings look synthetic and do not resemble the reference's packed groomed snow, tracks, and granular disturbed powder.
The requested active snow interaction is absent.

dimensions.reasons: The essential on-board relationship is present: detail_rider.png clearly places two blue foot/binding units atop the snowboard on the sloped snow. The rider and board are thus spatially related in the correct broad way.
issues: cam_submitted.png places the rider extremely small and distant, unlike the reference where the rider dominates the frame.
The standing/upright pose and horizontal board fail to match the reference's crouched edge changes and sharply lifted final board orientation.
Rocks are scattered on an upper hill instead of forming the close rocky snowbank behind the rider.
There is no trailing powder cloud behind the board tail.

dimensions.reasons: In detail_rider.png, the board length, two foot positions, and approximate rider height are broadly usable as a snowboard setup, and the boulders in cam_submitted.png are sensibly embedded in the slope.
issues: The rider's long rectangular limbs, very narrow torso sections, and oversized joint disks are not human proportions.
The boot/binding blocks are disproportionately boxy and tall relative to the thin board.
The main camera makes the subject tiny relative to the slope, unlike the intended rider-focused framing.

dimensions.reasons: Group A uses cool daylight-like illumination and produces distinct blue-gray shadows from the rider and board in wide_high.png and detail_rider.png. The snow, dark clothing, green board, and blue bindings are at least materially separated by color.
issues: Snow is pale and over-smoothed, with low contrast that obscures the surface in several views.
The rider's dark components are flat generic materials rather than varied fabric, matte helmet, reflective goggle lens, and padded outerwear.
The board lacks snow accumulation and a convincing dark glossy/used snowboard surface.
The lighting does not provide the strong realistic sunlit contrast and detailed terrain shadows visible in the reference.

dimensions.reasons: Visible submitted elements include the snowy slope, one rider-like figure, one snowboard, two blue foot/binding assemblies, and several rocks. These establish a partial inventory of the requested scene.
issues: No powder spray or loose snow burst is visible in any Group A render.
The black helmet, reflective goggles, padded jacket/hood, gloves, distinct snow pants, and detailed boots are missing or too abstract to count as successfully represented.
The rocky snowbank background is reduced to a few isolated low-poly boulders.
The key edge-driven carving and raised-tail action are not visibly represented by the static submitted scene views.

criteria.criterion: A continuous outdoor snow slope functions as the riding surface.
criteria.evidence: cam_submitted.png clearly shows the rider and board placed on a single broad white snow surface that rises steeply into the upper background without breaks.

criteria.criterion: One articulated human snowboarder is recognizable as the principal moving subject.
criteria.evidence: cam_submitted.png and wide_high.png show one central humanoid figure with a head, torso, two bent legs, two arms, and a snowboarding stance.

criteria.criterion: The rider stands on a recognizable elongated snowboard.
criteria.evidence: detail_rider.png clearly shows a long thin green-blue board with raised angular ends directly beneath the rider's two binding/boot assemblies.

criteria.criterion: The wider framing phases include a rough, partially snow-covered rocky bank beyond the riding surface.
criteria.evidence: cam_submitted.png contains several isolated dark faceted boulders scattered on the snow, rather than a substantial irregular rocky bank with visible snow patches above and behind the riding slope.

criteria.criterion: The rider reproduces the reference's black helmet and jacket with very dark navy or near-black snow pants.
criteria.evidence: The rider in cam_submitted.png and wide_high.png has a dark rounded head/helmet, very dark upper body, and near-black to dark navy lower limbs.

criteria.criterion: The snowboard is dark green-black and has two bindings with vivid blue accents.
criteria.evidence: detail_rider.png does show two vivid blue binding/boot assemblies, but the board top reads as bright teal/green-blue rather than the reference's dark green-black finish.

criteria.criterion: The snow surface shows granular variation, shallow ridges, and crossing track marks.
criteria.evidence: wide_front.png and wide_side.png show soft repeating wavy bands in the snow, but no clearly granular surface or distinct crossing board/ski-track pattern.

criteria.criterion: The major surfaces reproduce the reference's broad snow, winter-fabric, solid-board, and powder material response.
criteria.evidence: The rider components in detail_rider.png are smooth, uniformly faceted modeled pieces, and neither cam_submitted.png nor wide_high.png shows any airborne powder material response behind the board.

criteria.criterion: Feet, bindings, board, and slope maintain physically plausible attachment and contact.
criteria.evidence: detail_rider.png shows both lower legs terminating in the two blue boot/binding assemblies, which are seated on dark base plates attached to the board; the board is immediately against the snow surface.

criteria.criterion: The delivered project provides an editable rig that drives the snowboarder.
Continuous edge transitions drive linked curved turns with timing comparable to the reference.
criteria.evidence: Only still Group A renders are supplied, with no time-ordered frames showing board roll changes, a curved path, or linked edge-driven turns.

criteria.criterion: Body articulation communicates believable weight transfer during the turns.
criteria.evidence: The still views show one posed low-poly rider, but provide no temporal evidence of changing knee, hip, torso, and arm positions in response to successive turns.

criteria.criterion: Loaded carving produces a visible displaced powder plume from the snowboard's tail.
criteria.evidence: The visible board tail area in detail_rider.png is clear of spray, and no white powder plume trailing the board appears in cam_submitted.png or wide_high.png.

criteria.criterion: The animation follows the reference's ordered posture, edge-transition, and powder progression.
criteria.evidence: No submitted time sequence demonstrates the required progression from traverse through edge transition to a late low carve with a prominent trailing plume.

criteria.criterion: The camera reproduces the reference's readable rider scale, viewing angle, slope coverage, and lateral tracking.
criteria.evidence: In cam_submitted.png the rider occupies only a small portion of the lower-middle frame amid a very large empty slope, unlike the close readable reference framing; no temporal lateral camera following is evidenced.

criteria.criterion: Bright directional daylight creates strong snow highlights and distinct cast shadows.
criteria.evidence: wide_high.png shows a long, sharply defined dark rider-and-board shadow across brightly lit snow, and detail_rider.png also shows crisp directional shadows beneath the board.

criteria.criterion: The output video satisfies the requested container, codec, dimensions, frame rate, and approximate duration.
A usable editable Blender project containing the reconstructed scene and animation setup is delivered.
The rider has the reference-visible rounded helmet and eye-covering ski goggles.
criteria.evidence: The overview views show only a small dark rounded head with a red-orange accent, while detail_helmet.png does not clearly reveal the head or an eye-covering goggle construction; goggles are therefore not readable.

notes: The submission is recognizable as a simplified snowboarder standing on a board on a snow slope, with broadly matching board and binding colors. It falls far short of the reference's close realistic rider, detailed winter gear, rocky snowbank, carving pose, and powder spray; the floating brown block and weak/cropped evaluation views further reduce the result's quality.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
